snake-removal.intro: Darlington's snake work is Black Creek work. The creek's swamp corridor runs through the county seat's low side, and the town's snake population organises along it: black racers and rat snakes in the yards and outbuildings everywhere, banded watersnakes along the creek and the pond edges, and — the call that matters — cottonmouths in the wet ground near the swamp, thick-bodied and best identified from a distance. In town, most snake calls are rat snakes in crawlspaces, garages, and the occasional attic, hunting the rodents the older housing supports. Identification is the first service: in Darlington the harmless majority and the venomous minority live in the same postcodes, and the response differs completely by species.
snake-removal.extendedBody:
Reading a Darlington snake call

We start every Darlington snake call with the photograph or the description, because the county holds the full cast. Rat snakes — the long, climbing, grey-to-black snakes in the crawlspaces and attics — are nonvenomous, genuinely useful, and usually present because rodents are; a rat snake in the house is a rodent diagnosis delivered by a snake, and the removal comes with that conversation. Cottonmouths belong to the creek bottoms and pond edges: heavy-bodied, dark, reluctant to move, and the one local snake we will always advise distance on until it is in hand. Watersnakes along Black Creek are their harmless lookalikes, and telling them apart is a skill we are glad to demonstrate on the photograph you send. A snake inside the structure or a venomous snake established at the house is a removal; a racer passing through a yard is a sighting, and we will tell you which one you have before anyone drives anywhere.

faqs.q: There is a big dark snake by our Darlington pond. Is it a cottonmouth?
faqs.a: It could be — or it could be a banded watersnake, which is harmless and far more common at pond edges. Do not approach it to find out; take a photograph from a safe distance and send it to us, and we will identify it and tell you plainly whether it needs removing. A cottonmouth established at a pond edge a family uses is a removal call. A watersnake is a neighbour you can keep, and it eats the frogs and fish that draw the cottonmouths — one of the better arrangements a pond can have, once you know which snake you are looking at.

faqs.q: How much does snake removal cost in Darlington?
faqs.a: It depends on the species and the location — a rat snake located and removed from a crawlspace is a compact job; a venomous snake that has to be found in a swamp-edge yard is slower work. Identification from a photograph is free and comes first, because a share of Darlington's snake calls end with the snake identified as harmless and left in place, at no charge beyond the conversation. If removal is needed, we quote it before we come, and the visit includes the rodent or habitat reason the snake was there.

opossum-removal.intro: Darlington's opossums live off Black Creek and the town's older housing in equal measure. Virginia opossums den under the porches and in the crawlspaces of the county seat's pre-war homes, commute the creek corridor and the alley lines at night, and raise their litters under the quieter houses each spring. The town feeds them well — pet food, fruit trees, unsealed bins, and a creek full of everything an opossum eats — and they repay the neighbourhood in ticks eaten and snakes ignored, which is why our Darlington advice is usually about addresses, not animals: an opossum in the yard is a service, an opossum under the house is a tenancy, and only the tenancy needs ending.
opossum-removal.extendedBody:
The den is the problem; the animal is not

A Darlington opossum job is a closing job. The denning animal — often a female with young by spring — is trapped or excluded on the family's timing, because sealing a mother out and her litter in converts a small job into a dreadful one a fortnight later. Then the void closes: porch perimeters screened with mesh buried at the base, crawlspace vents and gaps repaired, the under-deck spaces that Darlington's older homes offer in abundance taken off the market. Opossums prospect proven dens, and a closed address stays closed while an emptied one is re-let by fall. Removal runs under the depredation permit for your property. The creek-side properties get the route conversation as well: an opossum's territory is drawn around its dinners, and pet food in at night and bins sealed redraws the map more cheaply than any fence — the animal itself will keep patrolling Black Creek's banks and eating the ticks there, which is where Darlington wants it.

faqs.q: How much does opossum removal cost in Darlington?
faqs.a: It depends on the den — one animal under a porch is a compact job; a crawlspace perimeter on an older home is more screening and more time. We inspect and quote the removal and the closing as one firm price, because in creek country an eviction without a screen is a vacancy posted. If the tenant is a mother with young, the timing is set around the family and the price quoted honestly for it, at the inspection.

faqs.q: An opossum visits our Darlington yard every night but lives somewhere else. Should we do anything?
faqs.a: Mostly, enjoy the service and manage the menu. A yard-visiting opossum that dens off your property is eating ticks, snails, and the occasional snake, and asking nothing but passage. The two things worth doing are keeping pet food indoors at night and sealing bins, so the visits stay visits and do not become a den search under your porch. If the route includes a dog that objects nightly, the food changes usually redraw the route within a week or two — opossums are loyal to dinners, not to yards.
